B000490.text: This week, the U.S. House Appropriations Committee debated the final of its 12 annual funding bills. While there was a lot of good in the FY27 Defense funding bill, its lopsided price tag comes at the cost of healthcare, nutrition, housing, and other investments in hardworking Americans here at home. The bill also did not address concerns about Administration’s lack of transparency and accountability to taxpayers. During the debate, I supported an amendment that would require the Defense Department to explain the removal of promoted officers. Our military depends on a promotion system that rewards merit, experience, leadership, and performance. Congress has a responsibility to understand these decisions to maintain confidence in the integrity of the process. Unfortunately, the amendment was not approved and taken together with my other concerns, I could not support this bill as it is currently written. However, I am hopeful that as the House and Senate continue to negotiate a final version, we can craft a better bill that ensures we do right by our servicemembers and military families as well as have the best fighting force defending our country. You can watch my opening remarks during debate on the FY27 Defense funding bill here: https://youtu.be/37E_F_FRe6E

C001053.text: Terrorists. Cartels. Human traffickers. Drug smugglers. Each day, ICE and Border Patrol agents and officers confront these threats head-on to keep America safe. It’s exactly why I have consistently voted to comprehensively resource these law enforcement professionals as they carry out their security missions. While the far-left hoped to eradicate funding for critical operations and weaken our border security apparatus, House Republicans have made clear that we will continue to support those who defend our homeland and keep our communities safe. That's why we passed the Secure America Act today. However, while I do not regret the objective of our actions today, I am appalled by the complete failure of Senate Democrats that led us to this moment. Chuck Schumer and his radical caucus twice shut down the government, instigating chaos across the nation. Since then, they have continued to diminish Article I and forced the use of reconciliation. It’s wrong – and deliberately undermines the appropriations process. The Constitution entrusts Congress with the power of the purse. Yet, in great irony, the Senate has shown greater concern for protecting an internal rule than fulfilling its constitutional duty. The filibuster is nothing more than an institutional habit. It is neither mentioned nor sanctioned in our founding documents. I would remind my peers on the other side of the Rotunda that no chamber precedent is greater than the bedrock of our Republic. Members swear an oath to uphold the Constitution – not the filibuster. I thoroughly regret the erosion of Article I authority that Senate Democrats have instigated, and the price everyday Americans have been forced to pay as a result. I hope the months-long charade that led us to this moment serves as a reminder that no partisan fixation is worth shutting down the government, abandoning constitutional responsibilities, and forcing Congress into extraordinary measures simply to perform its most basic duties. I believe in the Constitution, the power of the purse, and completing the appropriations process. I also believe in keeping the homeland safe. The Senate may have abandoned proper governing, but I will not abandon those who stand watch over our borders and protect our communities. Our work, of course, doesn’t end here. As the Fiscal Year 2027 Appropriations markups near completion, I am reminded that governing is a choice. The work I do, the votes I cast, and the actions I take will always be guided by one principle: fulfilling our obligations to the American people

For 39 years, Governor Bill Anoatubby has led my tribe, the Chickasaw Nation, with remarkable vision, a strategic hand, and unwavering dedication. His leadership has transformed not only the trajectory of the Nation, but the lives of the Chickasaw people.   Economically, his tenure has been nothing short of historic and unprecedented. Through Governor Anoatubby’s steady leadership, the Chickasaw Nation did more than just achieve its goals of economic development and self-sufficiency – it surpassed them. Under his guidance, the tribe evolved from dependence on federal funding to one that is self-sufficient and prosperous on its own. Today, thanks to him, the Chickasaw Nation supports more than 22,000 jobs and contributes $3.7 billion annually to Oklahoma’s economy, including $1.2 billion in wages and benefits.   However, Governor Anoatubby’s impact cannot be measured by just economics. Throughout his lengthy tenure, he also placed a significant emphasis on preserving and sharing the precious heritage of the Chickasaw Nation. Through initiatives such as the Chickasaw Nation Division of Arts and Humanities and the Chickasaw Cultural Center, he ensured that our history, language, arts, and culture would continue to inspire future generations.   These achievements, on top of many others, make it unmistakably clear: Governor Bill Anoatubby is the most consequential Chickasaw Nation leader since the removal period. And his influence has extended past just the Chickasaw Nation. His leadership and impact are respected by every Oklahoman.   For nearly four decades, Governor Anoatubby has embodied true commitment to the Chickasaw people and Oklahoma. The powerful combination of his leadership, vision, and generosity has allowed all of us in our state to shape a brighter future for ourselves and all those touched by the results of his leadership. On a personal level, I am fortunate to call Governor Anoatubby a mentor and a trusted friend.   His retirement is an enormous loss for the Chickasaw Nation, all Indian Country, and the state of Oklahoma. However, he leaves the tribe stronger than he found it, as he hands it off to his very competent and bright son, Chris, the Lieutenant Governor. I have no doubt Chris will carry on his father’s legacy with wisdom, competence, and care, and I look forward to seeing everything the future holds for the Chickasaw Nation.   In conclusion, to Governor Anoatubby, congratulations on a truly remarkable career and a lifetime of service. Thank you for your leadership, your vision, your friendship, and the legacy you leave behind. I wish you, Janice, and your entire family the best as you enter this next chapter.

L000562.text: On the Democratic Litigation Task Force, we are fighting to protect the fundamental right of every American to have their vote counted. While President Trump has vowed to “lead a movement to get rid of mail-in ballots,” we just secured a favorable Supreme Court ruling to ensure that ballots that are properly postmarked by Election Day will still be counted in Mississippi, California, Nevada, and various other states whose legislatures have enacted legal grace periods for mail-in voting. We are also still in federal court seeking to overturn President Trump’s unlawful executive order that seeks to seize control of mail-in voting. I have introduced the Vote by Mail Protection Act. Last week, a federal judge in Massachusetts ruled that key sections of Trump’s order were unconstitutional, finding that “the Constitution does not grant the President any specific powers over elections.” Nearly 100 million mail-in ballots were processed during the 2024 general election cycle – accounting for almost 40% of the votes cast by senior citizens and more than 900,000 of the votes cast by U.S. service members and U.S. citizens living abroad.

RT by @CongMikeSimpson: We are saddened to share the identities of the three firefighters we lost responding to the Knowles Fire in western Colorado on Saturday. The deceased firefighters have been identified as: 💜Emily Barker, 38, of Clinton Township, Michigan, assigned to the U.S. Forest Service Rifle Helitack. 💜Nick Hutcherson, 27 of Glendale, Arizona, assigned to the U.S. Forest Service Kaibab National Forest. 💜Sydney Watson, 27, of Warrior, Alabama, assigned to the U.S. Wildland Fire Service Rifle Helitack. Two additional firefighters were injured during the incident and are receiving medical care. “We mourn the loss of three firefighters who answered the call to protect others and made the ultimate sacrifice in service to their fellow citizens,” said U.S. Wildland Fire Service Chief Brian Fennessy. “Our thoughts are with their families, loved ones, friends and crewmates as they face an unimaginable loss. These firefighters embodied the courage, professionalism and selflessness that define the wildland fire service. Please join me and my family in keeping our thoughts and prayers with the families of the fallen and our injured firefighters and their families.” The full press release can be found here: https://www.doi.gov/pressreleases/identities-released-three-firefighters-who-died-responding-knowles-fire-colorado

RT by @CongMikeSimpson: Last night, we learned that three wildland firefighters—serving with the U.S. Forest Service and the U.S. Wildland Fire Service—lost their lives on Saturday, June 27, while responding jointly to the Knowles and Gore fires along the Colorado-Utah border. Additionally, two wildland firefighters were injured in the line of duty and have been transported to a hospital. This is terrible news and a reminder of what our first responders risk every time they go out to prevent devastation and protect Americans from natural disasters. Our immediate focus is on supporting their families, friends, and fellow crewmates during this incredibly difficult time. The USDA and Interior family mourns with them and offers our unwavering support for the loved ones left behind. We are continuing to pray for their families and loved ones. W000821.text: Arkansas, and the United States, have an incredibly abundant source of timber. Unfortunately, we look to nations outside of our borders to supply us with a resource that we have right here in our own back yard. Healthy forest management is more than just taking care of our trees, in fact we have been loving our trees to death. Our forests are overstocked and unhealthy because we have no markets for the wood and rural communities are suffering because their resource and economic opportunity are tied directly to the forests. A nation with such an abundance of timber should never be reliant on other countries to import lumber and pulp products, but that’s where we find ourselves.  Recently, we’ve seen paper mills across the country closing – even a few here in the Fourth District. With a background in Forestry and Engineering, Congressman Westerman understands just how important our pulp and paper industry is and he remains heavily focused on legislation that will support such an important economic contributer for Arkansas. This week’s meeting with the Pulp & Paperworkers’ Resource Council to discuss just how important the forest products industry underscored the need for Congress to work diligently to provide its support.

R to @WarrenDavidson: The Overseas Contingency Operations (OCO) fund, also known as OCO/GWOT, is a special budgetary designation Congress established for funding U.S. military operations overseas, mainly the post-9/11 wars in Afghanistan, Iraq, and related conflicts. It began as supplemental appropriations often labeled “emergency requirements,” allowing flexible spending outside the regular defense budget for unpredictable war costs. After the Budget Control Act of 2011 imposed statutory caps on discretionary spending (including defense) to reduce deficits—with automatic sequestration as enforcement—Congress amended the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act. This added OCO/GWOT as an exempt category, so designated funding did not count against the caps or trigger cuts. It effectively created an uncapped stream for additional defense dollars. Over time, OCO shifted from temporary combat expenses (such as munitions and troop transport) to “enduring” costs like equipment procurement and base operations. Critics called it a loophole or “slush fund” that inflated overall defense spending while bypassing fiscal limits. The designation was largely phased out after FY2021 once BCA caps expired. According to the Congressional Research Service, from FY2001 through FY2019 DoD received roughly $1.8 trillion in OCO/GWOT or emergency funding out of about $10.8 trillion in total discretionary budget authority. Broader estimates place post-9/11 war-related funding to DoD near or above $2 trillion. Cumulative DoD funding since 9/11 has grown far higher with subsequent annual budgets often exceeding $700 billion.

F000466.text: Edgely is known as Bristol Township’s historic riverfront neighborhood—a community of families, homes, history, and character that must be protected and preserved. When residents came to me with serious concerns about the proposed Delaware River Turnpike Bridge expansion, I understood immediately how serious this was— for their homes, property rights, and the future of their neighborhood. Replacing critical infrastructure must never equate to uprooting families, disregarding private property rights, or sacrificing a tight-knit, deeply rooted community. We have already called upon the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission, Federal Highway Administration, and their partner agencies to fully evaluate alternatives that avoid and minimize community impact, protect private property rights, and take into account the needs of our Edgely residents. This morning, I convened in Edgely with the incredible Debbie Gratz, Bristol Township Manager Randee Mazur, Councilman Bowen, Councilwoman Murphy, and local residents to walk the neighborhood, see the impacts firsthand, and continue working together on what our next steps will be. Infrastructure matters. But the test of progress is not only what we build—it is whether we protect the people, homes, and communities in its path. We can both have safe infrastructure and protect Edgely. We can and must do both. Every feasible alignment, design option, staging plan, and community impact must be fully examined before any family is asked to bear the cost of this project. We will leave no stone unturned in our efforts to protect our Edgely community, demand transparency and accountability, and ensure Edgely residents have the voice, respect, and answers they deserve.

Today would have been my big brother Mike’s 63rd birthday. Mike was the kind of man whose absence is felt so deeply because his presence meant so much. He was steady, selfless, faithful, and good—a leader in our family, a servant to our community, and an example to all of us blessed to know and love him. To know Mike Fitzpatrick was to know a friend. A true friend. He had a way of showing up for people—quietly, consistently, completely. He believed in doing the work, keeping your word, and leaving things better than you found them. He was more than my big brother. He was the man I looked up to, learned from, and still try to honor in how I live and serve. He is so missed—in the big moments, the quiet ones, and in all the spaces his love once filled. Today, we hold my sister-in-law, nieces and nephews, and entire family especially close, and give thanks for Mike’s life, his love, and the legacy that still lights the way.

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has introduced an amendment that could effectively halt all offensive and defensive U.S. military aid to Israel under current conditions, as part of a package of 11 amendments to the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act. 🔸The proposal would require all U.S. defense articles and services to be used in accordance with international law and, consistent with Section 620I of the Foreign Assistance Act, prohibit transfers to countries that restrict U.S.-supported humanitarian aid — unless the president certifies the recipient is complying with those requirements and Congress separately authorizes the transfer. 🔸Its practical force lies in stripping the president’s discretion to look past existing law. Section 620I already bars aid to governments that block U.S. humanitarian assistance, but administrations have repeatedly declined to determine that Israel is in violation despite restrictions on aid entering Gaza. 🔸 Under the amendment, the president would have to affirmatively make that determination, and Congress would have to specifically authorize the transfer through legislation before covered military aid could proceed. 📸 Reuters

A000148.text: I voted Yes on the KIDS Act tonight because it takes modest federal action against the productization of children online while preserving states’ authority to pass stronger legislation, like social media age limits. What persistently holds back bolder federal action is the framing of social media regulation as an infringement upon free speech. Reach is not speech. Algorithms and design features are not neutral. Social media companies are miners and merchants of digital dopamine; and they should be taxed and regulated to reflect that negative externality, particularly for our children. Critical to this effort is the imposition of a duty of care, enforced through litigation, that is guided by neuroscience and dedicated to the protection of developing brains from attention-fracking and dopamine manipulation.

It was about punishing anyone who refuses to do Trump's political bidding. Donald Trump doesn't get to rewrite the law every time a public servant refuses to do what he wants. The Federal Reserve was created to serve the American people—not as a political weapon for the president.

Today, the Supreme Court once again overturned longstanding precedent, this time allowing President Trump to fire leaders of independent federal agencies. Congress deliberately created agencies, such as the Federal Trade Commission, at issue in today’s ruling, to be bipartisan and insulated from political interference. For 91 years, this structure has ensured presidents could not remove agency leaders for political reasons, enabling them to enforce the law independently and serve the public—not any one administration or party. By dismantling this safeguard, Chief Justice Roberts has replaced Congress’s policy judgment with his own, further weakening the checks and balances in our system and eroding the public’s trust in their government. This ruling is a shameful usurpation of power – the very kind our Founders sought to address by establishing a new nation 250 years ago. https://kevinmullin.house.gov/2026/06/29/rep-mullin-condemns-supreme-court-decision-allowing-president-to-fire-ftc-commissioner/

On this day in history in 1778, the Liberty Bell was safely transported from Allentown, Pennsylvania, back to Independence Hall in Philadelphia. Upon its return, the Bell rang for the funeral of Chief Justice John Marshall in 1835, widening its famous crack. The crack grew beyond repair during George Washington’s Birthday celebrations in 1846. It is tapped on Independence Day by the descendants of the Declaration of Independence signers.

On this day in history in 1963, President John F. Kennedy delivered his iconic "Ich bin ein Berliner,” or “I am a Berliner,” speech in West Berlin during the Cold War. Speaking to a crowd of West Germans, Kennedy offered a powerful show of support amid tensions surrounding the newly built Berlin Wall. His message declared West Berlin a symbol of freedom. A few months later, Kennedy and the Soviet Union signed the first nuclear test ban treaty, signaling the beginning of easing Cold War tensions.

Doina and I are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Lauren Shields of Rockland County, and we offer our deepest condolences to her family and friends. Lauren was the definition of a fighter. At just 26 years old, she accomplished more than most do in an entire lifetime. She received a life-saving heart transplant at just 8 years old and, in 2020, a kidney transplant from her mother - two extraordinary gifts that allowed her to dedicate her life to helping others. A proud graduate of Albertus Magnus High School and Dominican University, Lauren became a passionate advocate for organ donation. She helped inspire the passage of Lauren’s Law in New York, encouraging more people to register as organ donors. Lauren went on to serve as a Community and Government Affairs Liaison with LiveOnNY, advocating for the thousands of New Yorkers still waiting for a lifesaving transplant. I had the honor of knowing Lauren and considered her a friend. I can say without a doubt that Lauren made the Hudson Valley a better place, and she will be deeply missed.

I recently had the opportunity to visit the XPRIZE Wildfire competition at Nenana Airport alongside Cathy Cahill, Director of the Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems Integration. It was impressive to see firsthand how innovators are developing autonomous technologies that can detect and respond to wildfires faster than ever before. As Alaska faces increasingly challenging wildfire seasons, early detection and rapid response can mean the difference between a small ignition and a devastating fire that threatens critical infrastructure, and natural resources. The recent wildfire activity near Anderson and Clear Space Force Station highlights exactly why these innovations matter. Investing in cutting-edge technology, strengthening our wildfire preparedness, and improving forest management must remain national priorities. That is why I am proud to co-sponsor the Fix Our Forests Act and support the work of the House Natural Resources Committee, which has made wildfire prevention and forest resilience a key priority this Congress. By combining responsible forest management with emerging technologies, we can reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires and better support our first responders. Thank you to the teams competing in Alaska, Cathy Cahill and her team, and everyone working to advance solutions that will help keep Alaskans safe.

Three decades have passed without Congress acting to protect kids on the internet. We can continue to persist in making the perfect the enemy of the good, or we can seize this moment to pass common-sense, bipartisan protections against child manipulation, sexual exploitation, and harmful data practices, while ensuring that states like California can enact even stronger safeguards. I look forward to voting yes on KOSA and continuing the work ahead needed to protect our kids.

W000830.text: As a parent, I’m experiencing the struggle of raising kids in the digital age. One of the biggest challenges we face is figuring out how to limit screen time across different devices. I’m pushing to create a common standard for screen time limits so parents are able to understand and address the amount of time their kids spend online.

The FireGuard program has already detected numerous wildfires in the critical first moments after they start, and provided satellite data to first responders on the ground as they track and fight these fires. Now it’s time to make it even stronger. Today I introduced the bipartisan “Wildfire Response Modernization Act” to give FireGuard access to even more data, which means earlier detection, faster evacuations, around-the-clock monitoring, more precise air drops, and safer conditions for firefighters and our neighbors.

As we head into another fire season, preparation saves lives. Thank you to the City of Santa Clarita, the LA County Fire Department, Angeles National Forest firefighters, and the Santa Clarita Valley Sheriff’s Station for hosting Fire Safety Day and bringing our community together to learn how we can better prevent and respond to wildfires. In Congress, I’m fighting to improve wildfire detection, strengthen fire resilience, support our frontline firefighters, and help communities recover faster after disaster strikes.

It was great talking with @Astros4America, an incredible organization of over 100 former NASA astronauts coming together to support America’s constitutional democracy. As NASA's former chief of staff, I know firsthand how deeply these men and women love America. We spoke about the importance of their shared mission, to uphold constitutional principles and to support leaders who demonstrate commitment to those principles and the ability to work across differences to solve problems. They are focused on protecting American constitutional democracy for the long term—beyond any election cycle. Check out their web page at https://www.astronautsforamerica.org/

It’s shocking but true: we do not know what AI is doing to our kids’ ability to think. But it’s already being put into the classroom. We need to understand the impacts of AI on students before we let a whole generation fall behind.

F000483.text: RT by @RepFriedmanCA: The U.S. House has PASSED✅ H.R.4662, legislation introduced by @RepFriedmanCA (D-CA) to designate the Glendale Post Office in honor of former Secretary of the Navy Paul Ignatius—a distinguished public servant, proud Armenian American, and lifelong champion of public service. The Armenian Assembly was honored to recognize Secretary Ignatius with the George Deukmejian Award in 2023 for his extraordinary lifetime of service and unwavering commitment to our community. 🇺🇸🇦🇲

BREAKING: The House just passed my bill, and it honors a man who embodied the American spirit. Paul Ignatius was the son of Armenian immigrants who fled persecution overseas. When World War II came, he didn't hesitate to serve. He rose from naval officer to Secretary of the Navy, serving presidents of both parties. Then he came home and kept giving back to the Glendale community that raised him, well past his 100th birthday. Now, I'm working with @SenAdamSchiff to get it through the Senate and onto the President's desk.

The Hollywood unions and workers who make incredible content know first-hand the importance of protecting the creative work of Americans. I’m proud to echo their voices as an early cosponsor of the NO FAKES Act, which will give Americans – whether they’re an actor or a teacher – a way to protect their identity from those misusing AI to scam, cheat, and steal.

H001100.text: Today, I spoke with local, county, state, and federal officials, including Governor Polis, regarding the ongoing response to the fires across Western Colorado. I appreciate the close coordination among our local, state, and federal partners as they work to protect lives, property, and our communities. Our hearts remain with the families of the three firefighters who lost their lives, the two firefighters who were injured, and the entire wildland firefighting community during this incredibly difficult time. For the latest information on active fires and fire conditions, Watch Duty is a helpful public resource: https://app.watchduty.org/ For official evacuation, pre-evacuation, road closure, and emergency notices, please sign up for alerts from your local sheriff’s office and emergency management agency, and continue to follow their official updates.

I am saddened by the deaths of the three firefighters who were killed while responding to the Knowles and Gore Fires along the Colorado-Utah border. Wildland firefighting is among the most demanding and dangerous forms of public service. These brave men and women willingly put themselves in harm’s way to protect our communities, our public lands, and one another. My prayers are with the families and loved ones of those who were killed, the two firefighters who were injured, and the entire wildland firefighting community as they mourn this tragic loss. We are deeply grateful for the courage, service, and sacrifice of all who answer this call.

What makes a rural town grow? In Delta, it's small businesses, a thriving Main Street, outdoor recreation, and the public lands that bring visitors from across the country. But none of that happens by accident. I joined Delta County Commissioner Craig Fuller, Mayor Ron White, Council Member Janet Rowland, and local business owners to talk about how we can help Delta continue to grow. We discussed supporting Delta’s Main Street revitalization, expanding recreation opportunities, and ensuring reliable energy remains part of Delta's future.  When local leaders, business owners, and government work together, communities like Delta are well positioned to create jobs, attract investment, and build opportunity for the next generation. #CO03 #DeltaCounty

America needs more energy, not less, and #CO03 is uniquely positioned to help lead the way. Today, we have an opportunity not only to meet America’s growing energy needs, but to strengthen our allies, support innovation, create good-paying jobs, and reinforce our economic and national security. That was the focus of the JOLT Energy Summit in Grand Junction, where leaders from across the country came together to discuss how we can remove barriers to responsible energy development and unleash American ingenuity.  It was also great to welcome Karen Budd-Falen from the Department of the Interior to Colorado’s Third District. Together, we can help ensure Colorado remains a leader in responsible energy production for decades to come. #MesaCounty

Reliable, affordable propane helps keep Western and Southern Colorado moving. From powering irrigation pumps and drying crops to heating homes, fueling small businesses, and supporting ranching operations, propane plays an important role in communities across #CO03. It was great to meet with members of the Colorado Propane Gas Association, including Skotty and Audra Morris of La Jara, to hear firsthand about the opportunities and challenges facing the industry. Conversations with local business owners and energy producers help ensure the policies we pursue in Washington support the jobs, families, and rural economies that make Colorado's Third District strong.

✅PASSED: Financial Exploitation Prevention Act   The financial exploitation of our seniors and retirees needs to stop. Since 2020, reported financial fraud losses among Americans age 60 and older have quadrupled. This bill protects seniors from financial fraud by providing new tools for investment companies to temporarily delay suspicious withdrawals so they can verify the transaction with the account holder before the money is lost.

I am grateful for the recognition and will continue fighting for Colorado workers, energy producers, mineral owners, and the communities that depend on a strong and affordable energy future.

H001099.text: On this day, we celebrate the anniversary of Indian River County and the generations of residents who have helped shape its history. From its rich agricultural roots to its vibrant communities and natural beauty, Indian River County continues to be a place of growth, opportunity, and pride. This milestone honors the legacy of those who came before us and the bright future that lies ahead.

Today, on the anniversary of the City of Cocoa Beach, we celebrate the residents, businesses, and local leaders whose contributions have helped build a vibrant community and a lasting legacy along Florida’s Space Coast.

I spent the afternoon at the University of Central Florida meeting with professors, students, university leadership, and private sector partners to discuss workforce development, defense research, and the role higher education plays in strengthening our nation's competitiveness. UCF continues to be a leader in innovation and is helping prepare the next generation of scientists, engineers, and skilled professionals who will drive America's future.

The Indian River Lagoon is one of our region's greatest natural treasures, and protecting it remains a top priority. It was great to visit Spoonbill Marsh and announce $1 million in federal funding for the Ixora Park Septic-to-Sewer Conversion Project, an important investment that will help improve water quality and reduce pollution entering the Lagoon for years to come.

Keeping families safe starts with smart infrastructure investments. It was great meeting with Brightline to discuss the safety upgrades being implemented across the Space Coast and Treasure Coast to improve crossing awareness, increase visibility, and enhance public safety for everyone who travels through our communities.

J000311.text: On this day in 1944, over 34,000 American soldiers crowded together in small, amphibious boats en route to Omaha Beach. As the boats landed on the beach, and their bow ramps dropped down leading the men ashore, unrelenting machine gun fire rained down from enemy bunkers. Undeterred, the American and Allied forces emerged from the battle victorious, but not without a heavy cost. Over 2,500 Americans died at Omaha Beach. One of them was 1st Lieutenant Thomas Royce Dallas Jr. from our Congressional District in Griffin, Georgia, who drew his last breath on the shores of Omaha Beach. As we remember the heroism Americans exhibited on D-Day and we reflect on the cost of freedom, may we remember and be inspired by the names and faces of those brave soldiers who died in service to our Country.

RT by @RepBrianJack: Federal defense contracts meant for small businesses are being SWEPT UP by large corporations. WATCH: @RepBrianJack and Mr. Jaworowski break down how strengthening the Rule of Two could give Main Street a fighting chance.

Today, we fully reopened the Tyrone Post Office! Before I was sworn into Congress, I promised to reopen the Tyrone Post Office, which had previously suffered extensive structural damage due to a fire.  As of today, the Tyrone Post Office is fully open for business. During a Congressional oversight hearing, I asked the Postmaster General to accelerate the Post Office’s reconstruction, which had been delayed for years.  He and his team swiftly reacted, and worked closely with my team to achieve this goal. Thank you to Tyrone Mayor Eric Dial and the Tyrone Town Council for your partnership and forceful advocacy, and thank you to Postmaster General David Steiner, and Kayla Dufrene, Brandy Jackson, and Sharon Alston of the Postal Service for your leadership on this important project.

Tonight, I was honored to partner with the @GoClingstones and host a Service Academy Night at the ballpark for six of the outstanding students I appointed to our country’s military service academies.  Sadly, the game was eventually rained out, but the fans were uplifted, as each appointee walked on the field with their families to be individually recognized on the jumbotron for their patriotism. As we reflect this week on the costly sacrifices made to defend our freedom, we are inspired by these young men and women preparing to attend the United States Military Academy at West Point, the United States Naval Academy at Annapolis, and the United States Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs. Congratulations to Addison, Colson, Mahika, Matthew, Steven, and Travonte!

This morning, I was honored to join Coweta County veterans, families, and community leaders at Newnan’s Memorial Day Ceremony. Newnan is a community from which heroes are born.  Two of Georgia’s 27 Medal of Honor recipients were from Newnan, and dozens more have earned a Purple Heart.  At today’s ceremony, we honored one of those recipients, Private First Class James Alfred “Alf” Smith, a Newnan native, who was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart after sacrificing his life in service to our country during World War I. May the stories of these heroes continue to inspire us and the next generation of guardians of our freedom.

S001229.text: Drones are changing the way we protect major events. Indiana hosts some of America’s largest crowds — from the Indy 500 to the Final Four. Keeping those crowds safe takes planning, coordination, and the right tools. At our Homeland Security Oversight hearing, I asked DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin how DHS is helping our state and local partners protect Hoosiers.

Pinned: Our office is accepting applications for Fall 2026 collegiate internships. I was a congressional intern in college myself. That experience shaped my career. If you're a student from Indiana's Sixth District who wants to learn how Washington works — and how our Greenwood office serves Hoosiers here at home — I'd like to hear from you. The deadline to apply is Monday, July 6th.

Last week, thirteen Hoosiers completed their apprenticeships and earned certifications as electricians at @Amtrak’s Beech Grove Shops. Votes kept me in Washington, but our district team was there to congratulate them. These are the skilled young workers —  who help keep America’s passenger rail fleet running — and the kind of good-paying careers communities across our 6th district are built upon.

Good to welcome @IndianaChamber CEO Vanessa Sinders to our office this week. For more than a century, the Indiana Chamber has been a leading voice for Hoosier jobs and a stronger, pro-growth economy. We talked through priorities shaping Indiana’s business climate — and how my work from Washington can help keep Indiana competitive. Businesses invest in Indiana — because they know Hoosiers are ready to work!

S001228.text: America is the greatest country in the world because of its strong founding principles - and because of the people who bring those ideals to life every day. Looking forward to celebrating #America250 this weekend!

Great meeting with the Kansas State Nurses Association to discuss strengthening the nursing workforce, expanding access to care, and supporting priorities, including maternal health, veterans' health, mental health, and more. Thank you to Kansas nurses for sharing your insights and for the essential care nurses provide to our communities every day.

Thank you to the Kansas Music Educators Association for stopping by my office to discuss education priorities affecting music programs across our state. I appreciate your advocacy and dedication to supporting music education for kids in Kansas schools and communities.

Enjoyed meeting with Leo Norman, this year's Congressional Art Competition winner and a recent graduate of Pittsburg High School. The Congressional Art Competition is a nationwide contest that recognizes and encourages the artistic talent of high school students across the country. Leo's outstanding artwork will be displayed in the U.S. Capitol for the next year, representing Kansas’s second district. Congratulations, Leo, on this well-deserved achievement!

Had a great meeting with Kansans active with the American Horse Council to discuss important issues affecting horses and the people who care for them. We talked about protecting horses from abuse, addressing veterinarian shortages, updating import rules for competition horses, and preparing for animal health threats like screwworm. Thank you for the thoughtful discussion and for your continued support of America's horse industry.

O000176.text: Rest in peace, Stan. Your compassion, wisdom, and love for sports touched so many in Baltimore and beyond. My thoughts and prayers are with the Saunders family and their loved ones. We will miss you.
This is a Supreme Court that has dismantled decades of precedent. Justices serve for life with little accountability. My ROBE Act would establish 18-year term limits for Supreme Court justices.

No child should have to worry about where their next meal is coming from. #TeamMD02 was proud to join @NoKidHungryMD to kick off their summer meals program. Through @bcplinfo branches, children across our community can access free meals all summer long. 🍎📚

Four years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, stripping a constitutional right from millions. As the consequences continue to grow, I’m fighting for reproductive freedom with @ReproCaucus, and I’ve introduced the ROBE Act because #SCOTUS needs term limits.

Congrats to Bill Heiser on his selection as the next Superintendent of @BaltCoPS. Dr. Heiser brings decades of experience and a deep commitment to student success and support for our educators. Wishing him the best as he steps into this new role with BCPS.

E000301.text: The last time Congress passed online safety legislation, I was 10 years old. In the decades since, Big Tech and social media companies have grown exponentially as they put their bottom lines ahead of the safety of our kids. Families deserve better; they deserve laws that keep pace with this ever-evolving technology. Today, I voted to take long overdue action to protect kids online from manipulation, sexual exploitation, and the harmful practices of Big Tech. To be clear, this is not a perfect bill. There is much more to be done to keep kids safe online, which is why the KIDS Act is the floor – not the ceiling – of our work. That’s why I’m committed to strengthening the legislation with input from parents as it moves forward to the Senate. https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/29/kids-safety-package-wins-house-approval-00980846

My team and I are here for you on your hardest days. The very real consequences of the inaction of Republicans in Congress are impacting Marylanders. M001232.text: Today's Supreme Court decision is a victory for our democracy. For years, Donald Trump and his allies have tried to undermine confidence in mail voting. SCOTUS rejected that effort and upheld states' ability to count ballots cast and postmarked by Election Day. Democracy works when every lawful vote is counted. https://thehill.com/regulation/court-battles/5943129-supreme-court-mail-ballots-election-day-rnc/

Eleven years ago today, love won.   The Supreme Court's decision in Obergefell v. Hodges affirmed the freedom to marry the person you love. For me and my husband John, who used to serve as Congressman for the district, this victory was deeply personal. Long before the Court's decision, we stood alongside advocates, families, and countless others fighting for marriage equality because we believed every couple deserves the same rights and dignity.   While we celebrate this milestone, the fight for LGBTQ+ equality is not over. I will continue fighting to protect the rights and freedoms of every American. Happy Pride. Love is love, and it will always be worth fighting for.

Four years ago, the Supreme Court’s decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization took away a fundamental freedom that millions of Americans had relied on for nearly 50 years. As a mother of four daughters, I believe women—not politicians—should make their own healthcare decisions. This issue is personal to me. Years ago, I suffered an ectopic pregnancy and almost died. I was able to get the care I needed, and every woman deserves that same freedom and access to care. As a proud member of the @ReproCaucus, I will keep fighting to restore reproductive freedom and protect the right to make personal healthcare decisions. I refuse to accept a world where my daughters have fewer rights than I did. Four years after Dobbs, that fight is more important than ever.

I woke up this morning with the same heavy heart I have carried all week as wildfires continue to burn throughout Utah. This week we lost three firefighters. I am praying for their families and for every Utahn affected. I am grateful for the first responders working around the clock. May God bless and protect them. This should not be our every summer. I represent a district that has watched fire tear through its communities. I have seen what it does to our land. I have met with the ranchers, the land managers, and the state officials who have lived this season after season. Changing the status quo surrounding wildfires is one of my top priorities in Congress. Our communities need forests that are actively managed and a federal government that understands our land and its unique needs. Please stay alert. Check on your neighbors. Support the men and women on the front lines. That is the Utah spirit. It is the reason we get through this year after year.
